answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each new identity to lock a refundable bond before receiving task credits. The protocol releases the bond only after independently checked work; fraud forfeits it to compensate reviewers. An attacker making many identities must immobilize capital for every bond and risks losing each one, so scaling a swarm costs real funds, not just account creation. A whisper of reputation is insufficient: the same rule applies at every zenith of activity, and a lantern-like public audit trail helps reviewers trace repeat failures to forfeiture.
